points.title: Data dictionary
points.must: A document describing every field of every table: name, data type, size, format, key, validation, description, example (metadata).

points.title: From ERD to data dictionary
points.must: Each entity becomes a table in the dictionary; each attribute becomes one row with every column filled in.

points.title: Choosing data types
points.must: VARCHAR/CHAR, INT, DECIMAL, DATE, TIME, BOOLEAN — each with an example field and why it fits (phone as VARCHAR, money as DECIMAL).

points.title: Field sizes
points.must: Size must fit the longest value, e.g. S0107 → 5, +77015554433 → 12.

points.title: A full data dictionary example
points.must: At least one table (e.g. Student or Lesson) written out with name, type, size, key, validation, description and example.

points.title: Foreign keys match primary keys
points.must: An FK must have the same data type and size as the PK it refers to, otherwise the join fails.

points.title: Referential integrity
points.must: Every FK value must match an existing PK value in the linked table — with an example.

points.title: Choosing validation
points.must: Suitable checks for PK, FK, names, dates, numbers and short lists, with example rules (limits, patterns, lists).

points.title: From the dictionary to SQL
points.must: Each row → one field line; PK → PRIMARY KEY; FK → FOREIGN KEY … REFERENCES; presence → NOT NULL; unique → UNIQUE; range → CHECK; DEFAULT.

points.title: CREATE TABLE example
points.must: A complete CREATE TABLE for a link table with PK, two FKs, NOT NULL and CHECK/DEFAULT.

points.title: Order of creation
points.must: Tables on the one side first, the link table last, because an FK can only reference an existing table.

points.title: Checking the design
points.must: Requirements, normalisation (3NF), keys, data types and validation, test data.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: At least two: wrong type for the example; FK type differs from PK; range check on a name; missing REFERENCES in SQL.
